label: Epic: Material Editor
title: Epic Games — Using the Main Material Node
focus: Read Material Inputs and Material Properties for enabled pins, defaults and the output node.
context: Unreal Engine 5.7 documentation; classroom project authored in 5.7.4.

label: Epic: Custom HLSL
title: Epic Games — Custom Material Expressions
focus: Read Using the Custom Material Expression: named inputs, return value, Output Type and the texture sampler example.
context: Unreal Engine 5.7 documentation; classroom project authored in 5.7.4.

label: Epic: material math
title: Epic Games — Math Material Expressions
focus: Look up Multiply, LinearInterpolate, DotProduct, Step and Sine. Check each input order and Sine Period.
context: Unreal Engine 5.7 documentation; classroom project authored in 5.7.4.

label: Epic: Material Instances
title: Epic Games — Material Instances
focus: Read Material Parameterization and Static Parameters. Ordinary value overrides differ from compile-time switches.
context: Unreal Engine 5.7 documentation; classroom project authored in 5.7.4.

label: Epic: texture data
title: Epic Games — Texture Asset Editor
focus: Find sRGB, channel preview, filtering and mip settings. Distinguish color images from numerical data.
context: Unreal Engine 5.7 documentation; classroom project authored in 5.7.4.

label: Epic: blend modes
title: Epic Games — Material Blend Modes
focus: Compare Opaque, Masked and Translucent, then locate Opacity Mask Clip Value.
context: Unreal Engine 5.7 documentation; classroom project authored in 5.7.4.

label: Epic: transparency
title: Epic Games — Using Transparency in Materials
focus: Read Using Transparency in Materials and Transparency Sorting. Check the material settings before adjusting Opacity.
context: Unreal Engine 5.7 documentation; classroom project authored in 5.7.4.

label: Epic: UVs and Panner
title: Epic Games — Coordinates Material Expressions
focus: Find TextureCoordinate, Panner, PixelNormalWS and VertexNormalWS. Match coordinate space to the calculation.
context: Unreal Engine 5.7 documentation; classroom project authored in 5.7.4.

label: Epic: PBR inputs
title: Epic Games — Physically Based Materials
focus: Read Base Color, Roughness, Metallic and Specular. Compare the material input with its lit appearance.
context: Unreal Engine 5.7 documentation; classroom project authored in 5.7.4.

label: Epic: Fresnel / DepthFade
title: Epic Games — Utility Material Expressions
focus: Find Fresnel for view-angle controls, or DepthFade for translucent intersections. These perform different jobs.
context: Unreal Engine 5.7 documentation; classroom project authored in 5.7.4.

label: Epic: world projection
title: Epic Games — Texturing Material Functions
focus: Read WorldAlignedTexture and WorldAlignedNormal. Check scale, coordinate conventions and the warning about moving objects.
context: Unreal Engine 5.7 documentation; classroom project authored in 5.7.4.

label: Epic: Single Layer Water
title: Epic Games — Single Layer Water Shading Model
focus: Read the implementation and material setup. Its Opaque/Masked blend setting can still produce a transparent-looking water surface.
context: Unreal Engine 5.7; this is an optional engine water model, distinct from the classroom water masters.

label: Epic: Content Examples
title: Epic Games — Content Examples
focus: Use the Materials and related example maps as a separate guided exploration. Follow the stations named in the course reference room.
context: Official sample project. Obtain a version compatible with your Unreal installation.

label: Ben Cloward: Shaders 101
title: Ben Cloward — Shaders 101, GDC 2016
focus: Read PDF pages 18–38 for UV scale, scrolling and layered distortion, and pages 54–67 for mask-based blending.
context: A historical talk explaining calculations shared by code and node editors; its screenshots are not UE 5.7 UI instructions.

label: Ben Cloward: tutorials
title: Ben Cloward — Shader tutorial videos and HLSL resources
focus: Use Shader Tutorial Videos for artist-focused node lessons and HLSL Training Videos for code.
context: Author-maintained resource index. Tutorial engine versions vary.

label: Iñigo Quílez: Palettes
title: Iñigo Quílez — Palettes
focus: Explore procedural palettes as an extension to choosing the colors in our banded study.
context: Optional extension. The classroom example uses explicit color parameters, not this article’s palette implementation.

label: Jettelly: Unity Shaders Bible
title: Fabrizio Espíndola / Jettelly — The Unity Shaders Bible
focus: Use Introduction to the Programming Language for HLSL and node concepts; Lighting, Shadows, and Surfaces for deeper lighting study.
context: Optional paid book with a publisher-provided sample. Unity HLSL, ShaderLab and Shader Graph require adaptation to Unreal; no purchase is required.

label: Book of Shaders: Color
title: Patricio Gonzalez Vivo & Jen Lowe — The Book of Shaders, Colors
focus: Try the Mixing color examples, then compare GLSL mix with HLSL lerp and Unreal Lerp.
context: Free interactive GLSL chapter; the engine wrapper differs from the classroom Three.js and Unreal projects.

label: Book of Shaders: functions
title: Patricio Gonzalez Vivo & Jen Lowe — The Book of Shaders, Shaping functions
focus: Start with Step and Smoothstep. Change the threshold or transition interval before combining operations.
context: Free interactive GLSL exercises; compare the argument order with Unreal nodes.

label: LearnOpenGL: Shaders
title: Joey de Vries — LearnOpenGL, Shaders
focus: Read Types, Ins and outs, and Uniforms after Ned’s presentation.
context: Ned’s final slide credits LearnOpenGL.com as diagram inspiration. This chapter is an additional course reading pointer, not a separate recommendation claimed from Ned.

label: LearnOpenGL: diffuse light
title: Joey de Vries — LearnOpenGL, Basic Lighting
focus: Read Diffuse lighting for the normal/light dot product. Our toon study adds thresholds and artist-selected colors.
context: An OpenGL lighting explanation, not Unreal’s complete Default Lit implementation.

label: Ned: original slides
title: Ned / NedMakesGames — Rasterization
focus: Download the unchanged guest presentation to annotate. Its final slide credits LearnOpenGL.com for diagram inspiration.
context: Original guest material supplied for this class; presented by Ned through screen sharing.

label: Mark Finch: GPU Gems water
title: Mark Finch — Effective Water Simulation from Physical Models, GPU Gems ch. 1
focus: Read 1.2 The Sum of Sines Approximation and the Gerstner Waves subsection, then 1.2.4 Texture Waves for surface detail.
context: Historical implementation with useful wave mathematics. The course pool grid is an original teaching study.

label: Rare: Sea of Thieves
title: Ang, Catling, Cifariello Ciardi & Kozin — The Technical Art of Sea of Thieves, SIGGRAPH 2018
focus: Read section 1.1 Ocean for the game’s FFT ocean, wave-peak color mask and foam art direction.
context: Documented production context. Our Gerstner study does not reproduce Rare’s FFT ocean.

label: Jeremy Birn: three-point light
title: Jeremy Birn — Three-Point Lighting for 3D Renderings
focus: Follow the key, fill and rim additions. Observe how illumination and separation change before adjusting material color.
context: Artistic lighting study; actual scene lights differ from our Unlit view-angle accents.

label: Pixar: Art of Lighting
title: Pixar in a Box / Khan Academy — Art of Lighting
focus: Explore lighting as a way to direct attention and support a scene’s visual intent.
context: Artistic further study, independent of the engine.

label: SimonDev: GLSL course
title: SimonDev — GLSL Shaders from Scratch
focus: Optional structured GLSL study alongside the numbered classroom examples.
context: Paid course; its lesson progression inspired the workspace organization. Supplied classroom code is original.

label: Simon Trümpler: tech art
title: Simon Trümpler / Simonschreibt — Tech Art Learning Materials
focus: Open My Document/Slides and its shader section for the Unreal-node and Unity-code teaching bridge.
context: A separate educator from SimonDev. Historical engine examples need current-engine adaptation.

label: Microsoft: HLSL functions
title: Microsoft — HLSL Intrinsic Functions
focus: Follow the per-function links for lerp, saturate, step, normalize and dot. Check arguments and return values.
context: Language reference; Unreal’s Custom node supplies its own input/output wrapper.

label: Khronos: GLSL reference
title: Khronos — GLSL 4.50 Specification
focus: Use the built-in function reference to cross-check the common arithmetic operations in the appendix.
context: Desktop GLSL reference. Browser WebGL uses GLSL ES, so version-specific features are not automatically portable.
